rows.note: Core harvest/structure paths are tested and the general Ultimate gap is closed by the default-branch gate. The remaining named gap is the source greenhouse matrix surface: upstream GreenhouseBE and LargeGreenhouseBE implement GreenhouseMatrixMember, and JDTE ships GreenhouseMatrixRuntime/ICreativeGreenhouse so a separate controller mod (jdte_matrix) can claim a greenhouse, drive its production profile and recognise a creative greenhouse that lives in that other mod. No counterpart exists for 1.20.1 — this repository contains no reference to it and no published 1.20.1 build was found — so porting the surface here would be dead code with no consumer. The row therefore stays **P** with a precise, non-actionable gap: the integration is missing because its only consumer is absent. Revisit only if a 1.20.1 controller mod appears.

rows.note: Verified 2026-11-02 on muse/forge-1.20.1-sender-validation: Ultimate cards verified by GameTest (ItemSenderUltimateGameTests, 11 tests) plus remaining-function GameTests (ItemSenderValidationGameTests, 9 tests): both Ultimate cards install with speed exclusivity, Ultimate Capacity gives Advanced 2500000 / Extended 5000000 FE (20000000 / 40000000 with 3 Capacity cards) and no measurable effect on Basic, Ultimate Overclock runs 10 ticker executions with the original base 64-per-execution normal cap (640/tick theoretical, stock-limited to 576), standard cost 25000 with direct-path deduction per moving execution and normal-path FE gate without per-operation deduction, redstone HIGH/LOW modes, Creative card (full 576 stock, zero FE), Underclock (one 64 batch per 40 ticks), area persistence and reach, Range scaling, refill throughput distinguishing 576 stock from 640/20000/100000 theoretical caps, and a SURVIVAL FakePlayer break of a non-default sender dropping exactly one self item per tier. Real Xvfb client opened all three GUIs (4/4/8 upgrade slots, 9 machine slots), GUI shift-click installed both Ultimate cards on Basic, creative tab and JEI contain all three senders and both Ultimate cards, baked models present. Packaged Forge 47.4.10 dedicated server (two JVMs) placed all three senders, live Basic transfer moved 576 stone, saved, chunk-unloaded and reloaded with Ultimate cards and FE intact (Advanced 1000000/2500000, Extended 1234567/5000000), fresh JVM restored Basic and Advanced with cards, FE and inventory intact, and SURVIVAL breaks dropped exactly one self item each (seed/verify markers in validation/forge-1.20.1-sender/dedicated-server). This round also fixed a real survival-break crash: vanilla destroyBlock removes the block entity before dropResources, and saveAdditional then touched dead capabilities; ItemSenderBE now caches its filter handler and the provider energy init skips on an invalidated provider. Known limits: the filter is GUI-present but inert in both original and port (parity quirk); PULSE mode is not exercised with a real rising edge; the 10000-per-execution direct cap is not saturated (largest measured single direct execution 2304). The other 27 Ultimate-restricted families are unchanged.

rows.note: Verified 2026-11-20: the last named gap — source coalesced accelerated processing — is implemented and tested. The brewer now implements CoalescedAcceleratedMachine, so Time Accelerator ticks aimed at it are accumulated and replayed as whole brew steps after the accelerator pass (processAcceleratedBrewing, ported verbatim from 1.21.1). EnergyUpgradeGameTests.coalescedAcceleratedTicksAdvanceWholeBrewStepsLikeTheSource drives the real water/wart step: 200 ticks leave brewProgress at 200 with no output, a further 200 complete exactly one step (real POTION of AWKWARD), the step pays 300 FE, and — matching the source — it buys one blaze charge when none is stored but never consumes it, because brew() is entered with a full bar; zero and negative submissions are no-ops. Earlier paths stay covered by the existing energy-brewing, fuel, copier and save/resume tests. Scope: the accelerated path is exercised for one step, not for the whole six-step chain under acceleration.
